title: Workflows default GitHub Actions cache-mode to none; grant read or write per job, never at job level as none
answers: conftest fails with 'Workflow must set top-level cache-mode: none'
new workflow job cannot restore or save the GitHub Actions cache
how do I grant a CI job access to the Actions cache
why is cache write denied for my job
body:
Invariant: every workflow file sets top-level `cache-mode: none`; a job gets cache access only through its own `cache-mode: read` (restore) or `cache-mode: write` (populate).
Enforced by .github/policy.rego:deny_top_level_cache_mode (denies a missing key, or any value other than `none`, for files with `jobs`) and .github/policy.rego:deny_redundant_job_cache_mode (rejects a job-level `cache-mode: none`).
Job-level values override the workflow default, so a job that needs no cache simply omits the key; writing `none` on a job is a policy failure.
What breaks if skipped: the conftest policy check fails for that workflow, or a job lacking a grant gets no cache and restores miss.
Constraints: the rules only fire when `input.jobs` exists, so composite action.yml files are not checked. The pinned actions/cache v6.1.0 does not read ACTIONS_CACHE_MODE, so `read` consumers of .github/actions/cache-hf log a `cache write denied` warning per run until @actions/cache 6.2.0 is released; that warning is expected and is not a reason to change the grant.
applies: Every workflow in .github/workflows/ that has a jobs block; not composite actions.
says: Our continuous integration policy check failed due to invalid workflow cache settings.
A newly created build job cannot restore or save shared dependencies from cache.
Grant read access to the shared build cache for our automated test suite.
Pipeline logs show a cache write denied warning during dependency restoration.
search: Every workflow file in .github/workflows/ containing jobs must set top-level cache-mode: none, with individual jobs explicitly specifying cache-mode: read or cache-mode: write for cache access. Enforced by .github/policy.rego via deny_top_level_cache_mode and deny_redundant_job_cache_mode, omitting cache-mode at the job level means no cache, while explicitly setting none on a job causes a conftest policy failure. These policy checks apply only when input.jobs exists and exclude composite action.yml files; additionally, read consumers of .github/actions/cache-hf log an expected cache write denied warning under actions/cache v6.1.0.
